knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 3.3.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Fraud flag: H₀ = genuine claim, H₁ = fraudulent. (1) Define Type I and Type II errors here. (2) In one sentence each, what are a p-value and power? (3) Refuse: 'I clicked a software z-test, so HT concepts are done' and 'HT foundations are the same skill as fitting a linear regression.'
knowledge_checks.body: Retrieve HT concepts on a vignette; refuse cookbook-as-concepts and regression conflation.
knowledge_checks.explanation: HT foundations are error types, p-value, and power — not software theatre or regression.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: (1) Type I: flag fraud when the claim is genuine. Type II: miss fraud when it is present. (2) p-value: probability under H₀ of data at least as extreme as observed. Power: probability of rejecting H₀ when H₁ is true. (3) Refuse: a cookbook software test does not replace HT vocabulary; linear regression is a different topic.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Swapping Type I/II, or treating a software z-test or regression fit as HT concepts.
success_criteria: Defines Type I/II, p-value, and power on the vignette.
